question: A user calls the help desk. What should you do before starting to troubleshoot?
options: Open or find the ticket and record the user's contact and issue
Remote into the PC at once without telling the user anything
Escalate straight to the network team so you can save your own time
Ask the user to reinstall the operating system first
explanation: Every interaction starts with a ticket: identify the user, record contact details, symptoms and impact. This keeps history and lets others pick up the case.

question: Two tickets arrive at once: the CEO's wallpaper is wrong, and the whole sales floor cannot print invoices. Which comes first?
options: The CEO's ticket, because of seniority
Whichever ticket has the longer and more detailed description
The sales floor, because more users and business are affected
The one that arrived a few seconds earlier, always
explanation: Priority follows impact and urgency, often defined in the SLA. A problem stopping many users from doing business beats a cosmetic issue, whoever reports it.

question: What does an SLA define for a help desk?
options: The brand of laptops the company buys
The passwords that technicians may share with each other on the team
The color scheme and logo of the ticketing system portal
Agreed service targets such as response and resolution times
explanation: A Service Level Agreement sets measurable commitments, for example first response within 1 hour for high-priority tickets and resolution within 8 hours.

question: In the CompTIA/Cisco troubleshooting method, what comes right after identifying the problem?
options: Implement the solution on all PCs
Establish a theory of probable cause
Escalate to the vendor immediately
Document findings and close the ticket
explanation: The order is: identify the problem, establish a theory, test it, plan and implement the fix, verify full functionality and document.

question: Your theory of probable cause was tested and proven wrong. What is the next step?
options: Apply the original fix anyway
Close the ticket as 'cannot reproduce'
Establish a new theory or escalate
Replace the user's PC with a new one
explanation: If the test fails, form a new theory (gathering more information if needed) or escalate to the next support level. You do not apply a fix that the test disproved.

question: Why should the ticket notes describe each step you tried, even the ones that failed?
options: Tickets are only valid if they are long
Auditors require at least ten written steps in every ticket you close
It helps others avoid repeating steps and builds the knowledge base
Failed steps are billed to the user's department at month end
explanation: Clear notes on what was tried, what worked and what did not save time for the next technician and feed knowledge base articles for recurring issues.

question: A frustrated user is shouting on the phone. What is the most professional response?
options: Put the call on hold until they calm down
Tell them firmly that the problem is their own fault and move on
Stay calm, listen actively and restate the issue to confirm
Hang up and send them a long email instead
explanation: Active listening, staying calm and paraphrasing the problem shows empathy and checks understanding. Arguing or hanging up escalates the situation.

question: When should a Tier 1 technician escalate a ticket?
options: When it exceeds their access, skill or SLA time
Only when the user asks to speak to a manager
Never, because Tier 1 must solve every ticket alone
As soon as any ticket is opened
explanation: Escalation is correct when the fix needs higher permissions or expertise, or when the ticket risks breaching the SLA. The escalation should include all notes collected so far.

question: Before opening a desktop PC to replace RAM, what should you do first?
options: Unplug the power and use an ESD strap
Keep it running so you can watch the change
Spray compressed air into the power supply
Remove the CMOS battery and leave it out
explanation: Disconnect power (and press the power button to drain residual charge), then ground yourself with an ESD wrist strap or mat to avoid damaging components.

question: Which fire extinguisher class is suitable for a burning server or other energised electrical equipment?
options: Class A (water)
Class C (CO2 or clean agent)
Class K (kitchen oils)
Class D (combustible metals)
explanation: In the US scheme, Class C covers energised electrical fires; CO2 or clean-agent extinguishers do not conduct electricity. In Europe the equivalent is CO2 marked for electrical risk.

question: Which Windows tool shows running processes and their CPU and memory use?
options: Event Viewer
Task Manager
Disk Management
Registry Editor
explanation: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) lists processes, performance graphs and startup apps. Event Viewer shows logs, and Disk Management handles partitions.

question: On a Mac, which app is the equivalent of Windows Task Manager?
options: Finder (file browser)
Disk Utility (drives)
Activity Monitor
Console (system logs)
explanation: Activity Monitor shows CPU, memory, energy, disk and network use per process. Console shows system logs and Disk Utility manages drives.

question: A PC restarted unexpectedly overnight. Where do you look for the cause on Windows?
options: Control Panel, Fonts
Device Manager, Ports section
Event Viewer, System log
File Explorer, Downloads folder
explanation: Event Viewer's System log records shutdowns, crashes (for example Kernel-Power or BugCheck events) and Windows Update restarts, with timestamps.

question: Which connector carries both digital video and audio and is common on TVs and projectors?
options: HDMI
VGA
DVI-A
PS/2
explanation: HDMI carries digital video and audio in one cable. VGA and DVI-A are analog video only, and PS/2 is an old keyboard/mouse port.

question: A user's laptop has a single USB-C port with a lightning-bolt icon. What does that icon usually mean?
options: The port is for charging only and has no data
The port can only connect to Apple devices
The port carries mains voltage and is dangerous to touch
Thunderbolt support for displays, docks and fast storage
explanation: The lightning-bolt logo next to a USB-C port marks Thunderbolt 3/4, which supports high-speed data, DisplayPort video, docks and power delivery over one cable.

question: A new monitor only has DisplayPort, but the old PC only has VGA. What is needed?
options: A plain DisplayPort-to-VGA cable with no electronics inside
An active digital-to-analog video converter
An HDMI splitter with two outputs
A USB-A to USB-B printer cable
explanation: VGA is analog and DisplayPort is digital, so you need an active adapter that converts the signal (here VGA to DisplayPort). A passive cable cannot convert between them.

question: A laptop feels slow and the drive LED is always lit. Task Manager shows the disk at 100%. Which upgrade helps most?
options: Replacing the HDD with an SSD
Adding a second keyboard
Changing the desktop wallpaper
Installing another web browser
explanation: A hard disk at constant 100% is a classic bottleneck. An SSD (SATA or NVMe) has far lower latency and greatly speeds up boot and application loading.

question: Which storage interface gives the highest speed in an M.2 slot?
options: SATA III
IDE/PATA ribbon
USB 2.0 Hi-Speed
NVMe over PCIe
explanation: An M.2 slot can carry SATA or PCIe. NVMe over PCIe lanes is several times faster than SATA III's 6 Gb/s limit. Check the slot type before buying.

question: A device shows a yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager. What does it usually indicate?
options: There is a driver or resource problem with the device
The device was disabled on purpose by the user or by a policy
The device is the fastest in the system
The device is a new, verified and signed peripheral
explanation: A yellow warning icon means Windows found the device but its driver is missing, wrong or failing. A down arrow means disabled.

question: Old laptops are being replaced. What should happen to the old drives and devices?
options: Throw them in the normal office bin to save time and money
Sell them online with the data still on them
Wipe or destroy data, then use certified e-waste recycling
Give them away to staff without checking the data first
explanation: Data must be securely erased or the drives destroyed, and electronics recycled through certified e-waste channels, because they contain hazardous materials and company data.

question: A PC gives no picture, no fans and no lights when the button is pressed. What do you check first?
options: The Windows activation status and product key
The installed graphics driver version
The power cable, outlet and PSU switch
The user's email and VPN password
explanation: With no signs of life at all, start at the power chain: wall outlet, power strip, cable, PSU switch and connections to the motherboard. Software cannot be the cause yet.

question: A user installed CAD software that crashes at launch on an older PC. What should you check early?
options: The app's minimum hardware requirements
The color and model of the PC case
The number of browser bookmarks
The keyboard layout and language setting
explanation: Compare the PC's CPU, RAM, GPU and OS version with the vendor's minimum requirements. Demanding apps often fail on hardware below spec.

question: A vendor's firmware update fixes a known bug in your laptops' docking stations. What is best practice?
options: Install it on every dock at once during work hours
Never update firmware once a device is deployed
Test on a few units, then roll out in a planned window
Ask users to download it themselves from any website they find
explanation: Firmware updates can brick devices if interrupted. Test on a pilot group, keep power stable and deploy in a maintenance window, using the vendor's official source.

question: What does the 'About This Mac' window show?
options: Running processes and their energy use
Saved Wi-Fi passwords for each known network and hotspot
macOS version, chip or CPU, memory and serial number
Network routes and the default gateway
explanation: About This Mac gives a quick summary of the macOS version, processor, memory and serial number, with a link to the full System Report.

question: A user changed their password but their PC still shows an old group policy. Which command pulls the latest policy?
options: sfc /scannow
ipconfig /renew
chkdsk /f
gpupdate /force
explanation: gpupdate /force reapplies computer and user Group Policy from Active Directory immediately. ipconfig /renew is for DHCP, chkdsk for disks and sfc for system files.

question: What is the difference between a security group and a distribution group in Active Directory?
options: Security groups grant permissions; distribution groups are for email lists
Security groups are only for printers; distribution groups for PCs
Distribution groups can log on to servers and run tasks; security groups cannot
They are the same object with two different names in the console
explanation: Security groups can be assigned permissions to resources (and can also receive mail). Distribution groups are used only for email distribution and cannot grant access.

question: A new employee needs access to the finance share. What is the best practice?
options: Give the user Full Control directly on the folder and all subfolders
Share your own login with the employee for a week
Copy all the finance files to the employee's desktop
Add the user to the finance security group that has the permission
explanation: Assigning permissions to groups (role-based access) and then adding users to the group is easier to manage and audit than per-user permissions.

question: Which service provides cloud identity for Microsoft 365, formerly called Azure AD?
options: Microsoft Entra ID
Google Workspace
Active Directory Domain Services
AWS IAM
explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) is Microsoft's cloud identity service. AD DS is the on-premises directory and AWS IAM controls access in Amazon Web Services.

question: A user who forgot their password calls in. What must you do before resetting it?
options: Email the new password to any address they give
Reset it immediately so the call stays short and the user is happy
Verify their identity using the approved procedure
Ask them to tell you their old password
explanation: Identity verification (for example a callback, employee ID or manager approval) stops social engineers from taking over accounts through the help desk.

question: A user must reach the departmental share \\fs01\sales as drive S: at every logon. What do you do?
options: Create a desktop shortcut to the server's IP address
Copy the share into OneDrive manually each day
Map a network drive with 'Reconnect at sign-in'
Install the share as a printer on the PC
explanation: Mapping the SMB share as a network drive with reconnect enabled (or via Group Policy or net use /persistent:yes) gives the user S: at each logon.

question: A user can open a file on a share but gets 'Access denied' when saving changes. What is the likely cause?
options: The network cable on the PC is unplugged
The DNS server for the whole company is offline
The monitor resolution is set too low
The user has Read but not Modify permission
explanation: Being able to open but not save points to permissions: the user (or their group) has Read on the share or NTFS folder but lacks Write/Modify.

question: A laser printer jams several times a day, always on the same tray. What is a sensible check?
options: The Windows display scaling of the users' PCs
The IP address, subnet mask and gateway of the printer
Paper type, humidity and worn pickup rollers on that tray
The SMB signing setting on the print server
explanation: Repeated jams from one tray usually come from wrong or damp paper, an overfilled tray or worn pickup/separation rollers. Network settings do not cause paper jams.

question: Jobs pile up in the print queue and nothing prints, although the printer is online. What is a quick fix?
options: Reinstall Windows on the print server from scratch tonight
Restart the Print Spooler service and clear the queue
Replace the printer's toner cartridge first
Change the user's screen saver
explanation: A stuck spooler often blocks the queue. Restarting the Print Spooler service (and deleting stuck jobs) usually releases it. Toner would produce faint or blank pages, not a stuck queue.

question: Printed pages from a laser printer come out with faded, uneven areas. What is the most likely cause?
options: A wrong IP address on the printer
The print queue was paused
A paper jam in the output tray
Low or failing toner cartridge
explanation: Faded or streaky output is usually low toner or a worn drum. Network or queue issues stop printing altogether rather than degrading quality.

question: In a Webex call, others cannot hear the user, but the headset works on another PC. What do you check first?
options: The app's microphone and OS privacy settings
The BIOS boot order and secure boot state of the laptop
The default printer driver on the PC
The DHCP lease time on the office router
explanation: Often the app is using a different input device or the OS blocks microphone access for the app. Check the audio device in Webex and the privacy/microphone permissions.

question: After a file server moved to a new IP, one PC still tries the old address while others work. What do you run on that PC?
options: netsh winsock reset
gpupdate /force
chkdsk C: /f
ipconfig /flushdns
explanation: The PC is using a cached DNS record. ipconfig /flushdns clears the local resolver cache so the next lookup gets the new address (also check the hosts file).

question: A desktop app connects to its server on other PCs, but on one PC it times out right after a security update. What is a good suspect?
options: A wrong time zone on the coffee machine
The refresh rate setting on the user's second monitor
An expired toner warning on the printer
A host firewall rule blocking the app on that PC
explanation: When one PC fails right after a change and others work, check the local firewall (for example Windows Defender Firewall) for a new rule or profile that blocks the app.

question: A laptop connects to Wi-Fi but lands on the guest network with no access to internal apps. What should you check?
options: The laptop's screen brightness
Which SSID the laptop joined
The battery health report
The keyboard language
explanation: Users often join the wrong SSID (for example Guest instead of Corp). Check the connected network and remove or deprioritise the wrong saved profile.

question: Which Linux command shows the IP addresses of all interfaces in modern distributions?
options: ipconfig /all
ip addr
netsh show ip
route print
explanation: The iproute2 command ip addr (ip a) shows interface addresses on Linux. ipconfig and route print are Windows commands; ifconfig is the older Linux/macOS tool.

question: On a Linux host you need to see which ports are listening and which process owns them. Which command fits?
options: ping -c 4 localhost
ss -tulpn
traceroute6 ::1
nslookup localhost
explanation: ss (from iproute2) replaces netstat: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -p process, -n numeric. On Windows the equivalent is netstat -ano.

question: A laptop asks for a BitLocker recovery key after a BIOS update. Where can the help desk usually find it?
options: Printed on the laptop's battery label
In the office router's DHCP lease table entry for that laptop
Inside the Windows Event Viewer System log
In Entra ID/AD or the user's Microsoft account for that device
explanation: BitLocker recovery keys are escrowed in Active Directory, Entra ID, MDM or the user's Microsoft account. Firmware or TPM changes often trigger the recovery prompt.

question: Windows keeps crashing after a new driver was installed, and it will not boot normally. What is a good next step?
options: Replace the motherboard straight away
Boot to Safe Mode and roll back the driver
Format the disk at once without taking any backup first
Disable the Windows firewall permanently
explanation: Safe Mode loads only essential drivers, so you can roll back the driver in Device Manager or use System Restore. Hardware swaps or formatting are last resorts.

question: A user's OneDrive icon shows a red X and files are not syncing. What do you check first?
options: The sync error and the user's sign-in state
The keyboard driver version and layout
The toner level of the default printer
The HDMI cable of the user's second monitor
explanation: Clicking the OneDrive icon shows the error: signed out, storage full, a blocked file name or a path too long. Fix that cause and sync resumes.

question: A user with a second monitor says the screen is 'stretched' and blurry. What do you adjust?
options: The Windows Update active hours for that PC
The power plan to High performance
Resolution, set to the native value
The default web browser
explanation: LCD panels look sharp only at their native resolution. In Display settings choose the recommended resolution and correct scaling for each monitor.

question: A web app shows old content and login loops only in one browser. What is a quick fix?
options: Replace the network card in the PC
Reinstall the operating system
Clear that browser's cache and cookies
Change the PC's IP address to a static one
explanation: Stale cached files or corrupted cookies often cause display issues and login loops limited to one browser. Clearing them (or testing a private window) confirms it.

question: A laptop goes to sleep after two minutes and drops Teams calls. Where do you change this?
options: Device Manager, Network adapters
Power and sleep settings
Disk Cleanup and storage options
Credential Manager in Control Panel
explanation: Screen and sleep timeouts are in Settings > System > Power (or the Control Panel power plan). Company policies may also set them through Group Policy or MDM.

question: A visually impaired user needs larger text and a screen reader on Windows. Where do you look?
options: BIOS/UEFI setup screen
Accessibility settings
Task Scheduler library
Windows Defender Firewall rules
explanation: Windows Accessibility settings include Narrator (screen reader), Magnifier, text size, contrast themes and more. macOS has VoiceOver and Zoom in Accessibility.

question: A Windows Update keeps failing with the same error code. What is a sensible step?
options: Disable updates forever on that PC
Delete the System32 folder to force a clean reinstall
Run the update troubleshooter and check disk space
Unplug the PC during the next update
explanation: Low disk space and corrupted update caches are common causes. The built-in troubleshooter, freeing space and searching the error code in the vendor KB are good first steps.

question: A Mac user cannot share their screen in a Webex meeting. What setting usually fixes it?
options: Change the items shown in the Finder sidebar
Turn off the Mac's Bluetooth
Allow Screen Recording for Webex
Reset the Mac's NVRAM every day
explanation: macOS requires explicit permission per app for screen recording, camera and microphone under System Settings > Privacy & Security. The app may need restarting after enabling it.

question: An external drive formatted on Windows as NTFS is read-only on a Mac. Why?
options: macOS natively reads NTFS but does not write it
The USB cable is too short
The drive is infected with malware that blocks writing
Time Machine has locked the drive
explanation: macOS can read NTFS but not write to it without extra software. For sharing between Mac and Windows, exFAT is the usual choice.

question: Which macOS feature makes automatic backups to an external disk?
options: AirDrop
Spotlight
Mission Control
Time Machine
explanation: Time Machine keeps hourly, daily and weekly backups on an external or network drive. AirDrop shares files nearby and Spotlight is search.

question: A user cannot AirDrop a file to a colleague's iPhone next to them. What should you check?
options: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and AirDrop visibility
The DNS server of the office network
The Windows activation key on the PC
The list of printers added on the Mac
explanation: AirDrop uses Bluetooth to discover and Wi-Fi to transfer. Both must be on and the receiver must accept from Contacts Only or Everyone (for 10 minutes on newer iOS).

question: A company phone stops getting work email after the user changed their network password. What is most likely needed?
options: Factory reset the phone right away
Replace the phone's SIM card
Update the password in the phone's mail account
Turn on airplane mode for an hour, then turn it off again
explanation: Mobile mail apps keep the old credentials and fail (sometimes locking the account). Updating the password in the account, or re-authenticating with modern auth, fixes it.

question: What does an MDM (Mobile Device Management) platform let IT do with company phones?
options: Increase the phone's battery capacity
Push policies and apps, and remotely lock or wipe
Make the phone work fully without any mobile network or Wi-Fi
Read users' personal messages by default
explanation: MDM (for example Intune) enrolls devices, enforces passcodes and encryption, deploys apps and Wi-Fi/VPN profiles and can remotely lock or wipe lost devices.

question: A phone charges very slowly or not at all with any cable. What simple check often solves it?
options: Reinstall all the apps on the phone
Change the phone's wallpaper and theme
Turn off automatic time zone
Clean lint from the charging port
explanation: Pocket lint packed in the USB-C or Lightning port stops the plug from seating fully. Gently cleaning it with a non-metallic tool often restores charging.

question: Which cloud service model gives users a finished application, such as Microsoft 365, with nothing to manage underneath?
options: IaaS
PaaS
On-premises hosting
SaaS
explanation: SaaS delivers complete applications. PaaS gives a platform to deploy your own code, and IaaS gives virtual machines, storage and networks that you manage.

question: What is a Type 2 hypervisor?
options: A type of SSD built for virtual machines
A hypervisor installed directly on server hardware
A cloud firewall placed between two VMs
Virtualization software running on a host OS
explanation: Type 2 (hosted) hypervisors such as VirtualBox or VMware Workstation run inside an OS. Type 1 (bare-metal) such as ESXi or Hyper-V Server run directly on hardware.

question: A user wants to install a free PDF tool from a random download site. What is the right response?
options: Point them to the approved company app store or request process
Let them, since free tools are always safe
Install it yourself with your own domain admin account right away
Disable antivirus so the installer runs
explanation: Unapproved sources often bundle adware or malware. Users should install from the company portal (Intune Company Portal, Self Service) or request the app through IT.

question: A user forwards an email 'from IT' asking them to confirm their password at a link. What do you tell them?
options: Reply with the password so IT can check it
Click the link but type a fake password to test it
Forward it to all colleagues as a warning
It is phishing: don't click, report it
explanation: IT never asks for passwords by email. Report the message (for example with the Report Phishing button) so security can block it for everyone; if they already clicked, reset the password.

question: Someone calls the help desk claiming to be a VP who is travelling and needs an urgent password reset to a new phone. What is this likely to be?
options: Social engineering using urgency and authority
A hardware fault on the VP's laptop
A DNS outage at the hotel
A normal request you should complete at once to help the VP
explanation: Pretexting with urgency and authority is a classic way to push the help desk past verification. Follow the identity procedure strictly, whoever the caller claims to be.

question: A user's browser suddenly has a new toolbar and the home page changed to an unknown search site. What do you do first?
options: Change the PC's IP address
Order a new laptop for the user straight away
Ignore it, because toolbars are harmless add-ons
Scan for malware and remove the extension
explanation: Browser hijackers are adware/potentially unwanted programs. Scan with the endpoint protection tool, remove the extension and reset browser settings.

question: Which of these is PII (personally identifiable information)?
options: An employee's name with their national ID
The company's public stock price
The SSID of the office guest Wi-Fi
The model number of a shared printer
explanation: PII identifies a person, such as national ID numbers, home addresses or medical records with names. It must be protected and shared only on a need-to-know basis.

question: Which password is the strongest?
options: Password123!Secure
Horse-battery-staple-91
Lisboa2026!Lisboa
qwerty12345678
explanation: Length matters most. A long passphrase with mixed words, case, symbols and digits is much harder to guess than short common patterns or dictionary words with a year.

question: A user notices someone they don't know following them through the badge door. What is this called?
options: Phishing
Tailgating
Spoofing
Shoulder surfing
explanation: Tailgating (piggybacking) is entering a secure area right behind an authorised person. Shoulder surfing is watching someone type, and spoofing is faking an identity or address.

question: An email shows the sender name 'Finance Team' but the address is finance@c0mpany-pay.com. What is this?
options: Spoofing of a trusted sender
A normal email from the finance team
A spam filter test sent by IT to every user
A DNS problem on the company's outgoing mail server
explanation: Display-name spoofing and look-alike domains (0 for o) are used to impersonate trusted senders. Check the real address and report it.

question: A user's account shows sign-ins from another country at night. What should the help desk do first?
options: Reset password, revoke sessions, check MFA
Wait for a week to see if it happens again
Ask the user to stop using email for a month
Delete the user's mailbox and archive
explanation: Signs of compromise call for containment: reset the password, sign out all sessions, review MFA methods and mailbox rules, then escalate to security.

question: Why should users lock their screen (Win+L) when leaving their desk?
options: To save printer toner and paper
To stop others using the open session
To speed up Windows Update
To refresh the PC's DHCP lease
explanation: An unlocked PC lets anyone walking by read data or act as the user. Locking is quick, and policies often auto-lock after a few minutes idle.

question: Which data class is a company's unreleased product design?
options: Public marketing
PII (personal)
Proprietary
Open source code
explanation: Unreleased designs are proprietary trade secrets. They must be labelled and shared only with authorised staff, unlike public marketing data.

question: A user received many identical unsolicited ads by email. What is the right action?
options: Mark them as spam/junk so the filter learns
Reply asking to be removed from the list
Click 'unsubscribe' in every message
Forward them to the whole department
explanation: Replying or clicking unsubscribe in unknown spam confirms the address is active. Marking as junk/spam trains filters and moves future messages away.

question: Which tool lets a technician view and control a user's Windows PC with the user's invitation and consent?
options: Disk Management console
Print Management console
Event Viewer
Quick Assist
explanation: Quick Assist (and the older Remote Assistance) lets the user share a code so a technician can view or control the session. RDP instead opens a separate session, usually without the user present.

question: Comparing RDP and VNC for remote support, which statement holds?
options: RDP is Microsoft's; VNC is cross-platform
VNC always encrypts traffic, RDP never does
RDP only works on Linux, VNC only on Windows
They are identical protocols with different logos
explanation: RDP (TCP 3389) is Microsoft's remote desktop protocol, typically opening a separate session. VNC (RFB, TCP 5900) mirrors the console screen and works across many OSes.

question: You paste a user's error log into a public generative AI chatbot to get help. What is the main risk?
options: The chatbot will crash the user's PC
Leaking confidential data or PII
AI tools never accept text longer than one line
The log will be printed on the office printer
explanation: Public AI tools may store or train on what you paste. Remove names, IPs, credentials and customer data, or use the company-approved AI tool, and still verify the answer.

question: An AI assistant gives a confident PowerShell command to fix a user's profile. What should you do before running it?
options: Ask the user to run it with admin rights for you
Run it immediately on all PCs to save time
Trust it, because AI answers are always verified
Verify it in trusted docs and test it
explanation: Generative AI can 'hallucinate' wrong or harmful commands. Verify each command against official documentation and test on a non-production machine before using it.

question: What is the difference between predictive AI and generative AI in IT support?
options: Predictive AI writes new text; generative AI only sorts tickets
Predictive forecasts; generative creates content
They are two marketing names for exactly the same technology
Generative AI only works offline on the PC
explanation: Predictive AI estimates outcomes from patterns (for example which disk will fail or ticket routing). Generative AI produces new text, code or images, such as drafting a reply.

question: Where should a help desk technician look first for a known fix to a recurring issue?
options: A random social media post
The user's personal notes and sticky notes
The company knowledge base
The printer's front panel
explanation: Internal KB articles document approved, tested fixes for recurring issues. Vendor KBs and forums come next, always checking that the source is trustworthy.

question: A remote user's PC is behind home NAT. Which remote support approach typically works without port forwarding?
options: Direct RDP from the help desk to the user's home IP
Telnet to the user's router on port 23
Pinging the PC until it answers
A cloud-brokered tool where both sides connect out
explanation: Tools like Quick Assist, Webex or TeamViewer have both technician and user connect outbound to a cloud relay, so no inbound port or VPN is needed.

question: A Windows PC gets an IPv6 address starting with fe80:: but no global IPv6 address, while IPv4 works. What does this show?
options: The PC has a public IPv6 address from the ISP
Only link-local; no RA or DHCPv6 arrived
The network adapter is broken and must be replaced
DNS is translating IPv6 names into IPv4
explanation: Every IPv6 interface creates a link-local fe80:: address by itself. A global address needs SLAAC from router advertisements or DHCPv6; if neither arrives, only link-local remains.

question: A user can browse the web but cannot reach the intranet app at 10.20.5.15. tracert stops at the user's own default gateway. What is the likely issue?
options: The user's monitor driver is outdated
The web browser cache is corrupted
DNS cannot resolve any public internet names
A routing or firewall block past the gateway
explanation: The PC reaches the gateway, and internet traffic works, so the local setup is fine. Traffic to the internal subnet is dropped after the gateway: a missing route or a firewall/ACL block.

question: A desktop beeps in a pattern at power-on and shows no image. What does this usually indicate?
options: A full print queue on the network
A POST error, often RAM or GPU
An expired Windows licence
A wrong time zone setting in Windows
explanation: Beep codes come from the firmware's power-on self test before the OS loads. The motherboard manual maps each pattern, commonly to RAM, graphics or CPU faults.

question: A user's laptop battery swells and the touchpad is pushed up. What is the correct action?
options: Keep using it on AC power until it gets worse
Stop using it and have the battery replaced
Puncture the battery to release the gas
Put the laptop in a freezer overnight to shrink it
explanation: A swollen lithium-ion battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it, keep it away from heat and have it replaced and disposed of as hazardous waste.

question: Which Windows command shows active TCP connections together with the owning process ID?
options: netstat -ano
ipconfig /displaydns
nslookup -type=mx
pathping -n
explanation: netstat -ano lists all connections and listening ports (-a), numeric addresses (-n) and the PID (-o), which you can match in Task Manager.
